title: BoJ opinions back faster hikes, one sees neutral rate 'considerably above 1%'
body: The Summary should firm pricing for a December hike to 1.5% and support the yen against the US dollar. It could also lift short-dated Japanese government bond yields, since the debate is now about pace, not direction. The member putting neutral considerably above 1% matters for terminal-rate pricing: it suggests markets could push their end-point expectations higher than the roughly 2% some already pencil in for next year. The dovish checks, notably weak consumption reinforced by today's 6.8% household spending slump, limit the case for a faster-than-quarterly pace for now. The view that the policy rate is already within the neutral range is the main counterweight. Higher oil prices, which members flagged as pushing up inflation, keep the energy link to BoJ policy live. --- The BoJ's argument is no longer about whether to keep hiking but how fast, and the hawks are making the louder case.

title: Japan household spending plunges 6.8%, 10th straight drop, as BoJ weighs December hike

That could temper the yen's gains from rate expectations in the near term. A strong hawkish tone in the Summary would likely outweigh one weak, volatile data point, leaving December pricing broadly intact. If the Summary instead shows members giving more weight to soft demand, the data would reinforce a slower path and leave the yen more exposed. Japanese government bond yields at the short end are the cleanest gauge of how markets weigh the two. --- Earlier: Event calendar in Asia Tuesday, November 10, 2026: BoJ and China trade data --- Japanese households are still keeping their wallets shut despite higher pay, giving the BoJ's cautious members fresh ammunition just as the hawks push for December.

title: US CPI preview: 43-day shutdown leaves no official annual rate as monthly pace seen easing
body: With no official annual rate, the monthly core reading carries most of the weight. A 0.3% core print would revive hawkish Fed pricing for December, likely lifting Treasury yields and the dollar and adding pressure to tech stocks still fragile after last week's selloff. A 0.2% or softer core reading would support the case for a pause and help extend Monday's equity rebound. Estimated annual headline figures near 4% may still dominate early headlines, so there is a risk of a knee-jerk move that fades once traders focus on the monthly detail. Lower gasoline prices during October offer some relief on the energy side. -- The monthly numbers should show prices rising more slowly than in September, but the shutdown gap means the annual inflation rate everyone quotes will be an estimate this time.

title: BlackRock: an AI spending slowdown in 2027 would hurt markets but could also lower yields
body: BlackRock's two-sided framing helps explain why Treasuries can act as a hedge against AI risk. A slowdown in AI spending would hurt equities but ease the competition for capital that has kept yields elevated. The shift in focus from suppliers to adopters suggests leadership could rotate away from chipmakers and infrastructure names over time, toward companies that show measurable productivity gains. The firm's question about whether traditional hedges still work, and its call for flexibility, argue against heavy directional bets until AI adoption data firms up. Its 2027 Global Outlook next month is the next marker for positioning. --- Earlier: Goldman sees $1.5 trillion in AI debt over three years, warns supply weighs on credit WSJ: Anthropic targets Nasdaq debut next week under ticker ANT despite tech selloff --- BlackRock says the easy part of the AI trade, betting the build-out would happen, is over, and the harder question now is whether adoption can pay for it.

Today's China trade data matters as a separate driver, since strong export demand linked to AI hardware could offer some support. Defensive currencies such as the yen and Swiss franc stand to benefit if AI volatility returns. The euro's inclusion among the bank's preferred currencies points to a broader rotation away from the US dollar rather than a pure flight to safety. Any concrete state-level action on data centres, particularly in Texas, is the main trigger to watch. --- AI has become a currency story, and Morgan Stanley's message is that when AI stocks wobble, the Australian dollar wobbles first.

title: Goldman sees $1.5 trillion in AI debt over three years, warns supply weighs on credit
body: For credit, Goldman's warning points to more pressure on spreads for AI-exposed investment grade names while the issuance pipeline stays this heavy. For equity investors, the shift in focus from demand to returns argues for more dispersion within the AI complex, rewarding companies that can show margin and free cash flow gains. Together with the wealth managers' calls to diversify, it adds to the case for broader market leadership. - Earlier: WSJ: Anthropic targets Nasdaq debut next week under ticker ANT despite tech selloff - The AI build-out is turning into a financing story, and Goldman's message is that balance sheets and returns, not demand, will decide who comes out ahead.

title: Japan Personal Spending Falls the Most in 6 Years
body: Japan's household spending fell 6.8% year-on-year in September 2026, a sharper decline than both August's drop and market expectations of a 3.1% decrease. This marked the tenth consecutive month of contraction and the steepest fall since September 2020, underscoring the drag from persistent inflation and rising borrowing costs. Spending weakened across most categories: food (-2.5% vs -1.4% in August), utilities (-10.5% vs -5.2%), healthcare (-7.6% vs -1.9%), education (-23.5% vs -12.3%), furniture and household goods (-6.4% vs -6.3%), and culture and recreation (-8.7% vs -4.3%). Outlays on transport and communication also slumped (-9.1% vs 0.2%), while the decline in clothing expenditure moderated (-3.6% vs -8.7%). Housing expenditure was unchanged after a 5.8% fall in August. On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, household spending declined 2.8%, reversing a 0.1% increase in August and missing forecasts for a 0.3% gain. It was the first month-on-month decline in three months. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Colombia Inflation Rate Hits Over 2-Year High
body: Colombia's annual inflation rate inched up to 6.30% in October 2026 from 6.29% in September, reaching its highest level since July 2024. The rate remained more than double the central bank's 3% target. Food prices accelerated to 7.31% from 6.74% in September, the fastest pace since November 2023. Inflation also picked up slightly in clothing and footwear (3.14% vs. 3.12%) and in information and communication services (4.47% vs. 4.45%). On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.20% in October, slowing from a 0.37% increase in September and marking the smallest monthly gain in three months. title: New Zealand Stocks Edge Higher in Morning Trade
body: The NZX 50 rose 17 points, or 0.1%, to 13,990 in Tuesday morning trading, reversing losses from the previous two sessions and following overnight gains on Wall Street driven by a rebound in AI-related stocks. Investors refocused on developments in the Middle East conflict and their implications for oil prices, while also awaiting the start of formal coalition negotiations after the release of the final election results, scheduled for November 27. title: Wall Street Rebounds on Tech Dip Buying
body: US stock indices rebounded on Monday from last week's sharp selloff, as renewed dip buying helped drive the market to its strongest session since April. The S&P 500 climbed more than 2%, the Dow advanced over 1,000 points, and the Nasdaq led the major averages with a gain of more than 3%. Chipmakers bounced back after Friday's steep decline, which followed Democrats' consolidation of control in Congress and stoked speculation about potential pressure on returns for AI companies, reinforcing existing worries about a slowdown in the sector's growth. AMD (+13%) was upgraded to "outperform" at Oppenheimer. Broadcom and Lam Research each rallied nearly 9%, Micron gained about 6%, and Applied Materials surged more than 11.5% ahead of its earnings report this week. Nvidia, however, fell 5% after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with an individual suspected of working as a Chinese spy, a development that could prompt Congress to consider tighter export controls on the company's chips. Among the major cloud and AI "hyperscalers," Alphabet (+2%) continued rolling out a broader lineup of AI chips. Meta jumped 5%, Microsoft rose 2.5%, and Amazon added 3.5%.
